guide.gettingStarted.title: Getting Started with BizManager
guide.gettingStarted.desc: Your first steps to setting up a fully operational ERP system
guide.gettingStarted.content:
BizManager is a comprehensive ERP platform designed for businesses operating in Qatar and Pakistan. To get started, first complete your Company Profile under Settings — enter your trade license details, CR number, tax registration (if applicable), and upload your company logo.
Next, configure your Chart of Accounts and set your base currency (QAR or PKR). Add your products or services catalog, then invite team members and assign roles.
The system supports multi-branch operations, multi-currency transactions, bilingual invoicing (English/Arabic or English/Urdu), and full compliance with local tax regulations including Qatar VAT and Pakistan FBR requirements.
Once your foundational data is in place, you can begin recording sales, managing inventory, and generating financial reports from day one.
guide.gettingStarted.tip: Complete the Company Profile and Chart of Accounts setup before adding products — this ensures all transactions are properly categorized from the start.
guide.dashboard.title: Dashboard Overview
guide.dashboard.desc: Your business command center with real-time KPIs, alerts, and quick actions
guide.dashboard.content:
The Dashboard provides a consolidated view of your business health at a glance. Key metrics include total revenue, net profit, outstanding receivables, payable obligations, and cash position — all updated in real time.
Access the Dashboard by clicking the home icon in the main navigation sidebar. Use the time period filters (Today, This Week, This Month, This Quarter, This Year) to adjust the reporting window.
The dashboard features interactive charts for revenue trends, expense breakdowns, and sales comparisons. The Low Stock Alerts panel highlights products below their reorder threshold, while the Recent Activity feed shows the latest transactions across all modules.
Top-selling products, overdue invoices, and pending approvals are surfaced as actionable cards so you can respond immediately without navigating away.
guide.dashboard.tip: Customize your dashboard layout by pinning the widgets most relevant to your role — managers may prefer financial KPIs while warehouse staff benefit from inventory alerts.
guide.sales.title: Sales Management
guide.sales.desc: Record sales transactions, manage customers, and track revenue performance
guide.sales.content:
The Sales module is where you record all revenue-generating transactions for your business. Navigate to Sales from the main sidebar to access the sales list, create new transactions, and view performance analytics.
Create a new sale by clicking 'New Sale', selecting products from your catalog, specifying quantities, and choosing the customer (or selecting Walk-in for anonymous sales). The system automatically calculates totals, applies applicable discounts, and computes tax.
Supported payment methods include Cash, Card, Bank Transfer, Credit (on account), and Split Payment. Each sale generates a unique reference number and can be linked to a delivery note or invoice.
The Sales Analytics section provides breakdowns by product category, customer segment, payment method, and time period, helping you identify trends and optimize your sales strategy.
guide.sales.tip: Link sales to registered customers to build purchase history profiles — this data powers the CRM and loyalty modules for targeted marketing.
guide.pos.title: POS Terminal
guide.pos.desc: Full-screen point-of-sale interface for fast retail checkout operations
guide.pos.content:
The POS Terminal is a dedicated full-screen checkout interface optimized for speed and ease of use in retail environments. Access it from the sidebar under Sales > POS Terminal, or navigate directly to the POS route.
Search products by name, SKU, or barcode using the search bar (keyboard shortcut F2). Add items to the cart with a single click, adjust quantities inline, and apply line-item or order-level discounts. The interface supports barcode scanner input for rapid item entry.
Payment processing supports Cash (with automatic change calculation), Card, Bank Transfer, and Split Payment across multiple methods. Upon completion, a receipt is generated that can be printed on thermal printers (58mm or 80mm) or shared digitally.
The POS maintains a session-based register that tracks opening balance, all transactions, and closing balance for end-of-day reconciliation. Hold orders allow you to park incomplete transactions and recall them later.
guide.pos.tip: Use the Hold Order feature (F4) during busy periods to serve multiple customers simultaneously without losing any transaction data.
guide.products.title: Products & Services
guide.products.desc: Manage your complete product catalog with pricing, images, barcodes, and categories
guide.products.content:
The Products module is your central catalog for all items and services your business offers. Access it from the sidebar to view, add, edit, or archive products with full detail management.
Each product record includes name, description, SKU, barcode (auto-generated or custom), category, unit of measure, cost price, selling price, tax applicability, and multiple images. Services can be flagged as non-stock items that skip inventory tracking.
Organize products into hierarchical categories and subcategories for easy navigation. The bulk actions toolbar lets you update prices, change categories, or adjust stock levels across multiple products simultaneously.
Advanced features include variant management (size, color, grade), composite products (kits/bundles), and integration with the Pricing module for tiered price lists and volume discounts.
guide.products.tip: Use the 'Duplicate Product' action to quickly create similar items — it copies all fields including images and variants, saving significant data entry time.
guide.inventory.title: Inventory & Stock Tracking
guide.inventory.desc: Monitor stock levels, movements, transfers, and warehouse operations in real time
guide.inventory.content:
The Inventory module provides real-time visibility into stock levels across all your warehouses and locations. Access it from the sidebar under Products > Inventory to view current quantities, movement history, and stock valuations.
Every stock movement is automatically recorded: inbound (purchases, returns from customers, production output), outbound (sales, returns to vendors, damage write-offs), and internal transfers between warehouses. Each entry is timestamped and attributed to the responsible user.
Set minimum stock thresholds and reorder points per product to trigger automatic low-stock alerts on the Dashboard. The Reorder Report identifies all items below their threshold and suggests purchase quantities based on historical consumption.
Stock valuation supports FIFO, LIFO, and Weighted Average costing methods. The Inventory Valuation report provides a snapshot of your total stock value for financial reporting purposes.
guide.inventory.tip: Schedule weekly cycle counts for high-value or fast-moving items to catch discrepancies early before they compound into significant variances.
guide.accounting.title: General Ledger & Accounting
guide.accounting.desc: Double-entry bookkeeping with chart of accounts, journal entries, and financial statements
guide.accounting.content:
BizManager implements full double-entry bookkeeping compliant with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS). Access the General Ledger from the Accounting section in the sidebar to manage your Chart of Accounts and journal entries.
The Chart of Accounts is organized into five major categories: Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, and Expenses. Each account has a unique code, name, type, and running balance. You can seed default accounts on first setup or create a custom structure.
Journal entries require balanced debits and credits before posting. Once posted, entries update all affected account balances immediately. The system prevents deletion of posted entries — use reversing entries for corrections.
Generate Trial Balance, Income Statement (Profit & Loss), Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow Statement at any point. All reports support date-range filtering and comparative period analysis (current vs. previous month/quarter/year).
guide.accounting.tip: Use recurring journal entry templates for monthly expenses like rent and utilities — this ensures consistency and saves time during month-end close.
guide.banking.title: Banking & Multi-Currency
guide.banking.desc: Manage bank accounts, reconcile statements, and handle foreign exchange transactions
guide.banking.content:
The Banking module lets you manage all your business bank accounts, track balances, and reconcile transactions with your accounting records. Access it from Accounting > Banking in the sidebar.
Add bank accounts with their account number, IBAN, SWIFT/BIC code, branch details, and opening balance. The system supports multiple currencies — common configurations include QAR, PKR, USD, EUR, GBP, and SAR with automatic exchange rate updates.
Bank reconciliation is streamlined: import your bank statement as CSV, then match imported transactions against recorded entries in BizManager. The system auto-matches by amount and date, leaving only exceptions for manual review.
Foreign exchange transactions are handled with real-time conversion rates. Realized and unrealized exchange gains/losses are automatically calculated and posted to the appropriate accounts during reconciliation.
guide.banking.tip: Reconcile your bank accounts at least weekly — the longer you wait, the harder it becomes to identify and resolve discrepancies.
guide.invoicing.title: Invoicing & Accounts Receivable
guide.invoicing.desc: Create professional invoices, manage quotations, and track customer payments
guide.invoicing.content:
The Invoicing module handles your entire accounts receivable workflow from quotation to payment collection. Access it from the Sales section in the sidebar to create invoices, quotations, and record incoming payments.
Invoices are auto-numbered (INV-00001 format) and include your company letterhead, customer details, line items, tax calculations, payment terms, and bank details. Supported payment terms include Immediate, Net 15, Net 30, Net 60, and Net 90 days.
The quotation workflow lets you create estimates that can be sent to customers for approval. Approved quotations convert to invoices with a single click, preserving all line items and terms. Track quotation conversion rates in the analytics section.
The AR Aging report categorizes outstanding invoices into Current, 1-30 days, 31-60 days, 61-90 days, and 90+ days overdue buckets, helping prioritize collection efforts. Payment recording supports partial payments and payment plans.
guide.invoicing.tip: Set up automatic payment reminder emails at 7 days, 14 days, and 30 days overdue — this significantly improves collection rates without manual follow-up.
guide.deliveryNotes.title: Delivery Notes & Shipping
guide.deliveryNotes.desc: Generate delivery notes, track shipments, and manage proof of delivery
guide.deliveryNotes.content:
Delivery Notes document the physical dispatch of goods to customers and serve as proof of delivery. Access the module from Sales > Delivery Notes in the sidebar to create, print, and track all outbound shipments.
Create a delivery note linked to a sales order or invoice, specifying items, quantities being shipped, vehicle/driver details, and delivery address. The system auto-generates a unique DN number (DN-00001 format) and supports partial deliveries against a single order.
Print delivery notes with full item details, customer signature lines, and your company branding. Digital delivery confirmation allows drivers or recipients to sign electronically, timestamping the proof of delivery.
Track delivery status through stages: Preparing, Dispatched, In Transit, Delivered, and Returned. The delivery history provides a complete audit trail of all shipments with dates, recipients, and confirmation status.
guide.deliveryNotes.tip: Always create delivery notes before dispatching goods — they protect your business in case of disputes about what was delivered and when.
guide.purchasing.title: Purchasing & Accounts Payable
guide.purchasing.desc: Manage purchase orders, vendor relationships, goods receipt, and bill payments
guide.purchasing.content:
The Purchasing module manages your entire procurement cycle from requisition to payment. Access it from the Purchasing section in the sidebar to create purchase orders, receive goods, and process vendor bills.
Purchase orders (PO-00001 format) flow through stages: Draft → Approved → Sent to Vendor → Partially Received → Fully Received → Billed. Each stage transition is logged with timestamps and responsible users for full auditability.
Goods Receipt Notes (GRN) record items received against a PO, updating inventory quantities automatically. The system flags discrepancies between ordered and received quantities for review before acceptance.
The Accounts Payable section tracks all vendor bills, payment due dates, and available early-payment discounts. The AP Aging report shows your payable obligations by due date, helping manage cash flow and maintain good vendor relationships.
guide.purchasing.tip: Negotiate early-payment discount terms with your top vendors (e.g., 2/10 Net 30) — even small discounts compound to significant annual savings.
guide.advancedInventory.title: Advanced Inventory & Manufacturing
guide.advancedInventory.desc: Bills of materials, work orders, assembly management, lot tracking, and bin locations
guide.advancedInventory.content:
The Advanced Inventory module extends basic stock tracking with manufacturing and warehouse management capabilities. Access it from Products > Advanced Inventory for BOM management, work orders, and location tracking.
Bills of Materials (BOM) define the components needed to assemble a finished product, including quantities, waste factors, and labor time estimates. Create multi-level BOMs for complex assemblies where sub-assemblies are themselves composed of raw materials.
Work Orders authorize the production of finished goods by consuming component inventory. Track work order progress through stages: Planned → In Progress → Quality Check → Completed. The system automatically adjusts component and finished goods stock upon completion.
Bin Location management organizes your warehouse into Zones, Aisles, Racks, and Bins for precise item placement. Lot and batch tracking assigns unique identifiers with expiry dates, supporting FIFO picking and full traceability from supplier to customer.
guide.advancedInventory.tip: Define accurate waste/scrap factors in your BOMs — this prevents unexpected stock shortages when actual production yields differ from theoretical calculations.
guide.pricing.title: Pricing & Promotions
guide.pricing.desc: Multi-tier price lists, volume discounts, promotional campaigns, and scheduled price changes
guide.pricing.content:
The Pricing module gives you complete control over your pricing strategy across different customer segments and market conditions. Access it from Sales > Pricing to manage price lists, discounts, and promotions.
Create multiple price lists (Retail, Wholesale, VIP, Distributor, Export) with different pricing levels for the same products. Assign price lists to customer groups so the correct pricing applies automatically during sales and invoicing.
Volume discount rules trigger price breaks at specified quantity thresholds (e.g., buy 10+ get 5% off, buy 50+ get 12% off). Promotional campaigns support percentage discounts, fixed amount reductions, buy-X-get-Y-free deals, and bundle pricing — all with configurable start/end dates.
The Price Calculator tool shows customers their best available price considering all active rules. Scheduled price changes let you plan future adjustments (e.g., seasonal pricing or supplier cost increases) that activate automatically on the specified date.
guide.pricing.tip: Review your pricing margins monthly using the Profitability Report — market conditions change and regular adjustments keep your business competitive and profitable.
guide.payroll.title: Payroll & HR Management
guide.payroll.desc: Employee records, salary processing, WPS compliance, leave management, and gratuity
guide.payroll.content:
The Payroll & HR module manages your workforce from hiring to separation, including monthly salary processing compliant with Qatar and Pakistan labor regulations. Access it from the HR section in the sidebar.
Employee profiles store personal details, contract terms, salary structure (basic + allowances), bank account information for salary transfer, and document copies (passport, visa, labor card). Upload employee photos for visual identification.
Monthly payroll processing calculates gross pay, overtime (as per Qatar Labour Law Art. 74 or Pakistan labor ordinances), deductions (advances, loans, absences), and net pay. Generate WPS-compliant salary files for bank submission in Qatar, or standard bank transfer files for Pakistan.
Leave management tracks annual leave entitlements (per Qatar Art. 79: 3 weeks for 1-5 years, 4 weeks for 5+ years), sick leave, and other absence types. End-of-service gratuity is automatically calculated per Art. 54 provisions based on tenure and final basic salary.
guide.payroll.tip: Process payroll before the 7th of each month to comply with Qatar WPS regulations — late salary payments can result in penalties from the Ministry of Labour.
guide.projects.title: Projects & Job Costing
guide.projects.desc: Project budgets, time tracking, expense allocation, and profitability analysis
guide.projects.content:
The Projects module enables detailed job costing and time tracking for service-based businesses, contractors, and project-oriented operations. Access it from the sidebar under Projects to create and manage active engagements.
Create projects with defined budgets, timelines, milestones, and assigned team members. Set budget categories for labor, materials, subcontractors, and overhead. The budget vs. actual dashboard shows real-time variance analysis as costs accumulate.
Time tracking supports both live timer (start/stop during work) and manual entry modes. Team members submit weekly timesheets for manager approval. Approved time entries automatically calculate labor costs based on employee hourly rates.
Material costs are allocated to projects when inventory items are issued or purchase orders are raised against a project code. The Profitability Report compares total revenue (invoiced amounts) against all allocated costs to determine project margin percentage.
guide.projects.tip: Use milestone billing to invoice customers at project checkpoints — this improves cash flow compared to billing only at project completion.
guide.communications.title: Communications & Messaging
guide.communications.desc: Payment reminders, customer notifications, message templates, and communication history
guide.communications.content:
The Communications module centralizes all outbound messaging to customers and vendors, ensuring consistent professional communication. Access it from the sidebar under CRM > Communications.
Send payment reminders to customers with overdue invoices — the system pre-fills relevant details (invoice number, amount, due date, days overdue) into customizable message templates. Reminders can be sent via email, WhatsApp, or SMS depending on your configured channels.
Message templates use placeholder variables (customer name, invoice number, amount, due date) that auto-populate when sending. Create templates for common scenarios: payment reminders, quotation follow-ups, delivery notifications, and account statements.
The Communication Log records every message sent with timestamp, recipient, channel, and delivery status. This audit trail helps resolve disputes and provides context when following up with customers about outstanding matters.
guide.communications.tip: Create a sequence of 3 escalating reminder templates (friendly → firm → final notice) and send them at 7, 21, and 45 days overdue for optimal collection results.
guide.security.title: Security & Access Control
guide.security.desc: Role-based permissions, custom access levels, audit logs, and user session monitoring
guide.security.content:
The Security module provides comprehensive access control to protect your business data and ensure users only access features relevant to their role. Access it from Settings > Security (owner access required).
BizManager uses a role-based access control (RBAC) system with granular permissions across all modules. Pre-built role templates include Owner (full access), Manager (operations + reports), Accountant (finance modules), Sales Staff (sales + POS), and Warehouse Staff (inventory only).
Create custom roles with precise permission combinations: each of the 24+ modules supports 6 permission levels (View, Create, Edit, Delete, Approve, Export). This means you can allow a user to view sales data but not create or delete transactions.
The Access Log tracks every login attempt (successful and failed), permission-sensitive operations, and data exports. Monitor active user sessions in real time, force-logout suspicious sessions, and set up automatic session timeouts for enhanced security.
guide.security.tip: Apply the principle of least privilege — grant users only the minimum permissions needed for their job function, and review access levels quarterly.
guide.reports.title: Reports & Business Intelligence
guide.reports.desc: Comprehensive financial, operational, and analytical reports with export capabilities
guide.reports.content:
The Reports module provides a complete business intelligence suite covering all aspects of your operations. Access it from the sidebar under Reports to choose from categorized report types.
Available report categories include: Sales Analytics (revenue by product/customer/period), AR Aging (receivables analysis), AP Aging (payables analysis), Payroll Summary (compensation overview), Inventory Valuation (stock worth), Stock Movements (quantity changes), Cash Flow (liquidity analysis), Purchasing Analysis (spend by vendor/category), and Profitability (margin analysis).
All reports support flexible date-range filtering, comparative period analysis, and drill-down from summary to transaction detail. Charts and graphs visualize trends, while data tables provide exact figures. Results can be exported to CSV or PDF format.
The Report Scheduler lets you configure automated report generation and delivery on daily, weekly, or monthly cadences. Bookmarked report configurations save your preferred filters for quick access to frequently-needed analyses.
guide.reports.tip: Schedule your most critical reports (Cash Flow, AR Aging, Sales Summary) for automatic weekly delivery — this keeps stakeholders informed without manual effort.
guide.data.title: Data Import & Export
guide.data.desc: Import data from QuickBooks, Sage 50, Tally, or export your BizManager data
guide.data.content:
The Data Import/Export module facilitates migration from other accounting systems and provides data backup capabilities. Access it from Settings > Data Import/Export in the sidebar.
Export any data set from BizManager to CSV format: Products, Customers, Vendors, Sales Transactions, Purchase Orders, Invoices, Employees, and Chart of Accounts. Exports respect your current filters and date ranges, and large datasets are automatically paginated.
Import data from popular accounting platforms including QuickBooks (IIF and CSV formats), Sage 50/Peachtree (CSV export), and Tally (XML format). The import wizard auto-detects file format, maps source fields to BizManager fields, and shows a preview before committing.
The Field Mapping interface lets you match source columns to destination fields, set default values for missing data, and configure data transformations (date format conversion, currency mapping, category assignment). Validation runs before import to flag duplicates and data quality issues.
guide.data.tip: Always perform a full data export before running any import operation — this creates a restore point in case the import produces unexpected results.
guide.monitoring.title: Real-Time System Monitoring
guide.monitoring.desc: Live system activity, active users, performance metrics, and operational health
guide.monitoring.content:
The Monitoring module provides real-time visibility into system usage and operational health. Access it from Settings > Monitoring to view live activity feeds and system performance indicators.
The Active Users panel shows who is currently logged in, which module they are using, and their session duration. The Activity Feed displays a live stream of significant operations (sales completed, invoices created, stock adjusted) across all users.
System health metrics include response times, database utilization, and API throughput. KPI tiles show today's key numbers (sales count, revenue, new customers, items shipped) with auto-refresh to keep the display current.
The Operations Timeline provides a chronological view of all system events, filterable by module, user, and event type. This is particularly useful for managers overseeing multi-branch operations or monitoring staff productivity during business hours.
guide.monitoring.tip: Display the monitoring dashboard on a dedicated screen in your office — it gives managers instant awareness of business activity without interrupting their workflow.
guide.companyProfile.title: Company Profile & Settings
guide.companyProfile.desc: Configure business identity, legal details, branding, and system preferences
guide.companyProfile.content:
The Company Profile is where you configure all business identity information that appears on invoices, quotations, delivery notes, and official documents. Access it from Settings > Company Profile.
Enter your company's legal name, trade name, CR/registration number, tax registration number (Qatar QID or Pakistan NTN/STRN), physical address, and contact details. Upload your company logo for document branding.
Configure operational settings: base currency, fiscal year start, default payment terms, invoice numbering format, and document language preferences. BizManager supports bilingual documents (English/Arabic for Qatar or English/Urdu for Pakistan).
Branch-specific settings allow each location to have its own address, phone, and operational parameters while sharing the same central database. The Branding section customizes document colors, fonts, and footer text for a professional appearance.
guide.companyProfile.tip: Keep your CR number and tax registration current in the system — these details print on official documents and must match your actual registration for legal compliance.
guide.tax.title: Tax Configuration & Compliance
guide.tax.desc: Configure VAT, sales tax, withholding tax, and generate tax returns
guide.tax.content:
The Tax module manages all tax-related configurations to ensure your business remains compliant with local regulations. Access it from Settings > Tax Configuration to set up tax rates, rules, and exemptions.
For Qatar operations, configure VAT settings (when applicable), customs duty tracking for imported goods, and excise tax for applicable product categories. For Pakistan operations, set up Sales Tax (standard 18%), Federal Excise Duty, Income Tax withholding, and Provincial sales tax rates.
Tax rules can be assigned at the product level, customer level, or transaction level. Exempt items, zero-rated supplies, and reduced-rate categories are all supported. The system automatically calculates applicable taxes during invoicing and purchase recording.
Generate tax return summaries with output tax (collected from customers) and input tax (paid to vendors) for the reporting period. The Tax Reconciliation report helps prepare your periodic filings by matching tax amounts to source transactions.
guide.tax.tip: Review tax configuration whenever regulations change — incorrect tax rates on invoices can create compliance issues and require costly manual corrections.
guide.budget.title: Budget Planning & Control
guide.budget.desc: Create departmental budgets, track variances, and manage financial planning
guide.budget.content:
The Budget module enables financial planning and expenditure control across your organization. Access it from Accounting > Budgets to create, monitor, and analyze budget performance.
Create annual budgets broken down by month, quarter, or custom periods. Assign budget amounts to specific Chart of Accounts categories (revenue targets and expense limits). Support for departmental budgets allows different teams to manage their own allocations.
Budget vs. Actual reports compare planned figures against real spending in real time. Variance analysis highlights over-budget categories with percentage deviations, helping managers take corrective action before overspending becomes critical.
Budget approval workflows require designated approvers to authorize budget proposals before activation. Revision history tracks all changes with justifications, providing an audit trail of financial planning decisions.
guide.budget.tip: Set up budget alerts at 75% and 90% consumption thresholds — early warnings give managers time to adjust spending before limits are exceeded.
guide.claims.title: Claims & Expense Management
guide.claims.desc: Employee expense claims, reimbursement workflows, and receipt management
guide.claims.content:
The Claims module handles employee expense reimbursement with a structured submission and approval workflow. Access it from HR > Expense Claims to submit, review, and process reimbursement requests.
Employees submit claims with expense category, amount, date, description, and attached receipt images (photo capture or file upload). Common categories include travel, meals, office supplies, client entertainment, and transportation.
The approval workflow routes claims to the designated approver based on department and amount thresholds. Approvers can approve, reject (with reason), or request additional information before processing. Approved claims are automatically added to the next payroll cycle or processed as standalone payments.
The Claims Dashboard shows pending approvals, total reimbursement amounts by category, and per-employee claim history. Policy compliance checks flag claims that exceed per-diem limits or fall outside approved expense categories.
guide.claims.tip: Require receipt attachments for all claims above your minimum threshold — this protects against errors and simplifies audit preparation.
guide.crm.title: CRM & Customer Management
guide.crm.desc: Customer profiles, purchase history, segmentation, and relationship tracking
guide.crm.content:
The CRM module provides a 360-degree view of your customer relationships, combining contact management with transaction history and engagement tracking. Access it from the sidebar under CRM to manage your customer database.
Customer profiles store company name, contact persons, addresses (billing and shipping), payment terms, credit limits, tax registration numbers, and custom fields. Link multiple contacts to a single customer account for organizations with multiple buyers or decision-makers.
The customer timeline shows every interaction: purchases, invoices, payments, quotations, communications, and support requests in chronological order. Purchase history analysis reveals buying patterns, average order value, payment reliability, and lifetime value.
Customer segmentation lets you group accounts by industry, geography, purchase volume, or custom criteria. Segments drive targeted pricing (price list assignments), communication campaigns, and prioritized service levels for your most valuable accounts.
guide.crm.tip: Set credit limits for customers who purchase on account — this prevents overexposure and keeps your accounts receivable at healthy levels.
guide.alerts.title: Alerts & Notifications
guide.alerts.desc: Configure system alerts for inventory, payments, approvals, and operational events
guide.alerts.content:
The Alerts module lets you configure automated notifications for critical business events so nothing falls through the cracks. Access it from Settings > Alerts & Notifications to manage your notification preferences.
Available alert types include: Low Stock (inventory below threshold), Overdue Invoices (past payment terms), Payment Received (customer paid), PO Approval Required (purchase order needs sign-off), Leave Request Pending (HR approval needed), and Budget Threshold (spending approaching limit).
Each alert type can be configured with recipient(s), delivery channel (in-app notification, email, or both), and trigger conditions (e.g., only alert for invoices overdue by more than 7 days or stock below 10 units). Priority levels (Low, Medium, High, Critical) determine notification urgency and visual styling.
The Notification Center in the top navigation bar shows unread alerts with quick-action buttons. Alert history provides a searchable log of all triggered notifications with timestamps and resolution status.
guide.alerts.tip: Configure critical alerts (cash shortage, major overdue receivable, system security) to send email notifications — in-app alerts only work when users are actively logged in.
guide.branches.title: Multi-Branch Management
guide.branches.desc: Manage multiple business locations, inter-branch transfers, and consolidated reporting
guide.branches.content:
The Multi-Branch module enables businesses with multiple locations to operate from a single unified system while maintaining branch-level segregation where needed. Access it from Settings > Branches to configure and manage your locations.
Each branch has its own address, contact details, warehouse(s), and optionally its own bank accounts and tax registrations. Users can be assigned to specific branches, restricting their data access to only their location's transactions.
Inter-branch stock transfers move inventory between locations with full tracking: the sending branch creates a transfer-out, and the receiving branch confirms receipt. Transfer-in-transit tracking prevents stock from being 'lost' between locations.
Consolidated reporting aggregates data across all branches for company-wide views, while branch-specific reports isolate performance by location. The Branch Comparison dashboard shows side-by-side metrics (revenue, expenses, inventory value) across all your locations.
guide.branches.tip: Designate a central warehouse as your distribution hub for inter-branch transfers — this simplifies logistics and provides a single point of inventory control.
guide.warranties.title: Warranty & After-Sales Service
guide.warranties.desc: Track product warranties, service requests, and after-sales support records
guide.warranties.content:
The Warranty module tracks post-sale obligations and service commitments for products sold with warranty coverage. Access it from Sales > Warranties to register, monitor, and process warranty claims.
Warranty registration links a sold product (by serial number or invoice reference) to coverage terms: start date, duration, coverage type (full replacement, parts only, labor included), and any exclusions. Registration can happen automatically at point of sale or manually after delivery.
When a customer reports an issue, create a Service Request linked to the warranty record. The system validates coverage status (active, expired, or excluded) before proceeding. Service requests track issue description, diagnosis, resolution, parts used, and labor time.
The Warranty Dashboard shows active warranties by product category, upcoming expirations (for proactive outreach), and service request metrics (average resolution time, common issues, warranty cost analysis). This data helps improve product quality and manage after-sales costs.
guide.warranties.tip: Use warranty expiration data proactively — contact customers before warranty expires to offer extended coverage or maintenance plans, generating additional revenue.
guide.loyalty.title: Loyalty & Rewards Program
guide.loyalty.desc: Customer loyalty points, reward tiers, redemption rules, and engagement programs
guide.loyalty.content:
The Loyalty module helps you retain customers and encourage repeat purchases through a configurable points-based rewards program. Access it from CRM > Loyalty Program to design and manage your loyalty scheme.
Configure earning rules that award points based on purchase amount (e.g., 1 point per QAR/PKR spent), specific product purchases (bonus points on featured items), or visit frequency. Points accumulate on customer accounts and are visible on receipts and customer portals.
Design reward tiers (Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum) with escalating benefits: higher earning rates, exclusive discounts, priority service, or free shipping thresholds. Customers automatically upgrade or maintain tier status based on spending within defined qualification periods.
Redemption rules define how points convert to value: direct discount at checkout, free products from a reward catalog, or voucher generation. Set minimum redemption thresholds and expiry periods to maintain program sustainability and encourage timely usage.
guide.loyalty.tip: Send personalized notifications when customers are close to earning a reward or upgrading their tier — this creates urgency and drives incremental purchases.
tutorial.first_sale.title: Making Your First Sale
tutorial.first_sale.steps.1: Navigate to Products in the sidebar and add at least one product with a name, price, and initial stock quantity.
tutorial.first_sale.steps.2: Go to Sales from the sidebar and click the 'New Sale' button in the top right corner.
tutorial.first_sale.steps.3: Use the product search to find and select items from your catalog. Adjust quantities as needed.
tutorial.first_sale.steps.4: Select a customer from the dropdown or leave as 'Walk-in Customer' for anonymous sales. Verify the total.
tutorial.first_sale.steps.5: Choose a payment method (Cash, Card, or Bank Transfer), confirm the amount received, and click 'Complete Sale' to finalize.
tutorial.setup_accounting.title: Setting Up Your Chart of Accounts
tutorial.setup_accounting.steps.1: Navigate to Accounting > General Ledger and click 'Seed Default Accounts' to populate the standard chart of accounts.
tutorial.setup_accounting.steps.2: Review each account category (Assets, Liabilities, Equity, Revenue, Expenses) and customize names and codes for your business.
tutorial.setup_accounting.steps.3: Go to Settings > Company Profile and set your Fiscal Year start date (e.g., January 1 or April 1).
tutorial.setup_accounting.steps.4: Enter opening balances for each account by creating an 'Opening Balance' journal entry with the effective date as your go-live date.
tutorial.setup_accounting.steps.5: Post the opening balance entry and verify the Trial Balance shows zero difference between total debits and credits.
tutorial.create_invoice.title: Creating Your First Invoice
tutorial.create_invoice.steps.1: Navigate to Sales > Invoicing and click the 'New Invoice' button to open the invoice creation form.
tutorial.create_invoice.steps.2: Select a customer from the dropdown — their billing address, tax number, and default payment terms will auto-populate.
tutorial.create_invoice.steps.3: Add line items by searching for products or services. Set quantities, unit prices, and any applicable discounts per line.
tutorial.create_invoice.steps.4: Review the calculated totals (subtotal, tax, discount, grand total) and set payment terms (Immediate, Net 15, Net 30, Net 60, or Net 90).
tutorial.create_invoice.steps.5: Click 'Save as Draft' to review later, or 'Save & Send' to finalize the invoice and deliver it to the customer via email.
tutorial.manage_payroll.title: Processing Monthly Payroll
tutorial.manage_payroll.steps.1: Go to HR > Payroll and verify all employee records are up to date with correct salary structures, bank details, and active status.
tutorial.manage_payroll.steps.2: Click 'Run Payroll' and select the payroll month. The system calculates base pay, allowances, overtime, and deductions automatically.
tutorial.manage_payroll.steps.3: Review each employee's payslip details — verify overtime hours, deductions (advances, loans, absences), and net pay amounts.
tutorial.manage_payroll.steps.4: Make any manual adjustments (bonuses, one-time deductions) then click 'Approve Payroll' to lock the run.
tutorial.manage_payroll.steps.5: Export the WPS file (for Qatar banks) or bank transfer file (for Pakistan) and submit to your bank for salary disbursement.
tutorial.inventory_setup.title: Setting Up Inventory Management
tutorial.inventory_setup.steps.1: Go to Products > Warehouses and create your physical storage locations with names, addresses, and manager assignments.
tutorial.inventory_setup.steps.2: Navigate to Products and create your category hierarchy to organize items logically (e.g., Electronics > Phones > Accessories).
tutorial.inventory_setup.steps.3: Add products with complete details: name, SKU, cost price, selling price, initial stock quantity, reorder point, and preferred warehouse.
tutorial.inventory_setup.steps.4: Generate barcodes for each product using the Barcode tool — print labels using the batch printing feature for physical labeling.
tutorial.inventory_setup.steps.5: Perform an initial physical stock count using the Cycle Count feature and reconcile any differences between system and actual quantities.
tutorial.import_data.title: Importing Data from Other Software
tutorial.import_data.steps.1: Navigate to Settings > Data Import/Export and select the 'Import' tab to begin the import process.
tutorial.import_data.steps.2: Choose your source system (QuickBooks, Sage 50, Tally, or Generic CSV) and select the data type to import.
tutorial.import_data.steps.3: Upload your exported file (IIF for QuickBooks, CSV for Sage 50, XML for Tally) using the file upload area.
tutorial.import_data.steps.4: Review the field mapping preview — the wizard auto-maps recognized fields, but verify custom fields and fix any flagged validation errors.
tutorial.import_data.steps.5: Click 'Confirm Import' to process the data. Review the import summary showing successful records, skipped duplicates, and any errors.
tutorial.setup_company.title: Configuring Your Company Profile
tutorial.setup_company.steps.1: Navigate to Settings > Company Profile and enter your legal company name, trade name, and registration numbers (CR, Tax ID).
tutorial.setup_company.steps.2: Upload your company logo (recommended 400x400px PNG with transparent background) for use on all printed documents.
tutorial.setup_company.steps.3: Enter your full business address, phone numbers, email, and website. For multi-branch setups, this is your head office address.
tutorial.setup_company.steps.4: Configure operational preferences: base currency, fiscal year start, default invoice terms, and document language (English, Arabic, Urdu).
tutorial.setup_company.steps.5: Review the preview of how your details appear on invoices and delivery notes, then click 'Save' to apply all settings.
tutorial.create_delivery.title: Creating a Delivery Note
tutorial.create_delivery.steps.1: Navigate to Sales > Delivery Notes and click 'New Delivery Note' to start documenting an outbound shipment.
tutorial.create_delivery.steps.2: Link the delivery to an existing invoice or sales order by searching and selecting the reference number.
tutorial.create_delivery.steps.3: Verify or adjust the items and quantities being shipped — for partial deliveries, reduce quantities to match what is actually being dispatched.
tutorial.create_delivery.steps.4: Enter shipping details: vehicle number, driver name, delivery date, and any special handling instructions or notes.
tutorial.create_delivery.steps.5: Save and print the delivery note. Hand one copy to the driver and keep one for your records. Update status to 'Dispatched' when goods leave.
tutorial.run_pos.title: Using the POS Terminal
tutorial.run_pos.steps.1: Open the POS Terminal from Sales > POS or use the direct navigation link. Open your cash register by entering the opening balance.
tutorial.run_pos.steps.2: Add products to the cart by searching (press F2 to focus), scanning barcodes with a USB scanner, or browsing category tiles.
tutorial.run_pos.steps.3: Adjust quantities using the +/- buttons or type directly. Apply discounts at item level or order level as needed.
tutorial.run_pos.steps.4: Select the payment method (Cash, Card, Split). For cash, enter amount received and the system calculates change automatically.
tutorial.run_pos.steps.5: Click 'Complete Sale' to finalize. The receipt prints automatically (if printer configured) or can be shared digitally. Repeat for next customer.
faq.how_reset_password: How do I reset my password?
faq.how_reset_password_answer: Passwords are managed inside Farooq BizManager. To change your own password, open your Profile. If you forgot your password, ask the company owner: in Users & Roles they can click the key button next to your name and set a new one. If the owner forgot their own password, follow the "Forgot owner password" section of the setup guide (README) on GitHub.
faq.how_add_user: How do I add a new team member?
faq.how_add_user_answer: Navigate to the Team page from the sidebar. Click 'Add User' and enter their full name, email address, and assign an appropriate role (Owner, Manager, Accountant, Sales Staff, etc.). For multi-branch setups, also assign their branch location. They will receive an invitation email with instructions to create their account and set a password.
faq.how_backup_data: How do I backup my business data?
faq.how_backup_data_answer: Go to Settings > Data Import/Export and select the 'Export' tab. Choose which data types to include (Products, Customers, Sales, Vendors, Employees, Chart of Accounts). Click 'Export' to download CSV files for each selected category. We recommend performing weekly exports and storing them in a secure cloud location like Google Drive or OneDrive for disaster recovery purposes.
faq.how_change_language: How do I change the interface language?
faq.how_change_language_answer: Click the language/globe icon in the sidebar footer area. Select your preferred language from the available options: English, Arabic (العربية), or Urdu (اردو). The interface will switch immediately and your preference is saved to your user profile. Arabic and Urdu modes also switch the layout to right-to-left (RTL) for comfortable reading.
faq.how_generate_barcode: How do I generate barcodes for my products?
faq.how_generate_barcode_answer: Go to Products, open any product detail view, and click the 'Generate Barcode' button. You can generate EAN-13, Code-128, or QR Code formats. For bulk operations, select multiple products from the list view, then click 'Batch Barcodes' from the actions menu to generate and print label sheets compatible with standard label printers (Avery or thermal).
faq.how_create_role: How do I create a custom user role with specific permissions?
faq.how_create_role_answer: Navigate to Settings > Security & Roles (requires Owner access). Click 'Create Custom Role' and give it a descriptive name. The permission matrix shows all modules (rows) against actions (columns): View, Create, Edit, Delete, Approve, Export. Check the boxes for each permission combination this role should have. Save the role, then assign it to users from the Team page.
faq.how_reconcile_bank: How do I reconcile my bank statements?
faq.how_reconcile_bank_answer: Go to Accounting > Banking and select the bank account to reconcile. Click the 'Reconciliation' tab and import your bank statement CSV file (download from your internet banking portal). The system will auto-match transactions by amount and date. Review auto-matched entries, manually match remaining items, and mark any bank fees or charges as new transactions. Click 'Complete Reconciliation' when the difference is zero.
faq.how_track_expenses: How do I track business expenses?
faq.how_track_expenses_answer: There are two methods depending on the expense type. For vendor bills (rent, utilities, supplier invoices), create them under Purchasing > Vendor Bills. For employee reimbursements (travel, meals), use HR > Expense Claims where employees submit receipts for approval. Both methods automatically create accounting entries debiting the appropriate expense account. Use the Expense Analysis report to monitor spending by category.
faq.how_run_reports: How do I generate and schedule business reports?
faq.how_run_reports_answer: Navigate to Reports from the main sidebar. Choose from 9+ report categories: Sales Analytics, AR Aging, AP Aging, Payroll Summary, Inventory Valuation, Stock Movements, Cash Flow, Purchasing Analysis, and Profitability. Select your desired date range and any filters (branch, category, customer). Reports display interactive charts and detailed data tables. Click 'Export' for CSV/PDF download, or use 'Schedule' to set up automatic recurring delivery.
faq.how_use_pos: How do I set up and use the POS terminal?
faq.how_use_pos_answer: Navigate to Sales > POS Terminal to open the full-screen cashier interface. First-time setup: open a register session by entering your cash opening balance. To process a sale, search products using F2 (supports name, SKU, and barcode), add items to cart, adjust quantities, and select payment method. Press Enter or click 'Complete Sale' to finalize. At end of day, close the register to reconcile cash against recorded transactions.
faq.how_delivery_note: How do I create and manage delivery notes?
faq.how_delivery_note_answer: Go to Sales > Delivery Notes and click 'New Delivery Note'. Link it to an existing invoice or sales order. Select the items and quantities being shipped (supports partial deliveries). Add vehicle, driver, and logistics details. Print the delivery note for the driver to carry. When delivery is confirmed, update the status from 'Dispatched' to 'Delivered' with the confirmation date. The customer's invoice will reflect the delivery status.
faq.how_tax_setup: How do I configure tax rates for my business?
faq.how_tax_setup_answer: Navigate to Settings > Tax Configuration. For Qatar businesses: set up VAT rates (standard, zero-rated, exempt categories). For Pakistan businesses: configure Sales Tax (standard 18%), FED, income tax withholding rates, and provincial variations. Assign tax profiles to products (taxable, exempt, zero-rated) and customer types (registered, unregistered, government). The system automatically applies correct tax during invoicing based on these configurations.
faq.how_loyalty_program: How do I set up a customer loyalty program?
faq.how_loyalty_program_answer: Go to CRM > Loyalty Program and click 'Configure Program'. Set your earning rules (points per currency unit spent), define tier levels with qualification thresholds and benefits, and configure redemption options (points-to-discount conversion rate, minimum redemption). Once activated, points are automatically calculated and awarded with every sale linked to a registered customer. Customers see their points balance on receipts.
faq.how_multi_branch: How do I manage multiple business locations?
faq.how_multi_branch_answer: Navigate to Settings > Branches and click 'Add Branch' for each location. Configure each branch with its address, contact details, assigned warehouse(s), and local settings. Assign users to branches from the Team page. Use inter-branch transfer orders to move stock between locations. The consolidated dashboard shows all-branch totals, while branch filters on reports let you analyze individual location performance separately.
